title: Deploy Runbook: Search Service
text: Steps to deploy the search service: build the image, run migrations, roll out to canary, then promote to full fleet.

title: Rollback Runbook: Search Service
text: How to roll back the search service: identify the last known-good release, redeploy it, then invalidate caches.

title: Runbook: Scaling Search Replicas
text: Steps to scale search replicas: increase the replica count, wait for warmup, then shift traffic gradually.

title: FAQ: Rate Limiting Search API
text: Rate limit rules for the search API: 100 requests per minute per key, burst up to 20, 429 on excess.

title: FAQ: Search API Authentication
text: Authentication setup for the search API: bearer tokens issued by the auth service, rotated every 90 days.

title: Incident: Cache Stampede Outage (2024-03)
text: What caused the cache stampede outage: a cold cache after deploy plus no request coalescing caused a thundering herd on the database.

title: Postmortem Follow-up: Cache Stampede Action Items
text: Remediation items from the March incident: introduced request coalescing and a warm-start step before traffic cutover.

title: Incident: Cache Stampede Recurrence (2025-02)
text: A recurring cache stampede issue resurfaced in February 2025 despite the 2024 fix; the new region had not received the coalescing patch.

title: Incident: Search Latency Spike (2025-04)
text: Why did search latency spike recently: a slow query plan regression in the reranker after a dependency upgrade.

title: Postmortem Follow-up: Latency Spike Root Cause
text: Deep dive into the April regression: an unindexed join in the new candidate-merge path caused the slowdown. Reverted and added a guardrail test.

title: Incident: OOM Crash in Indexer (2023-11)
text: Root cause of the indexer OOM crash: an unbounded batch size on a large corpus import caused the indexer to exceed its memory limit.

title: Postmortem Follow-up: OOM Crash Fix Verification
text: Verification pass on the November indexer regression: batch sizes are now capped and memory usage is tracked during ingestion.
